Order
The present third application has been filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of bail in connection with Crime No.139 of 2023 registered by Police Station Madhoganj, District Gwalior for offence under Sections 376, 376(2)(n), 376-D, 377, 323 and 506 of IPC.
As per the case of the prosecution, the allegation against the present applicant is that he committed rape upon the prosecutrix, who is a married lady.
On the basis of such allegation, the above crime was registered.
It is further submitted that in the said subsequent offence, since the charge sheet was filed and cognizance was taken by the trial Court, the bail was cancelled.
The cancellation order was challenged before the the Apex Court in SLP(Crl.) No.13738 of 2024, which was dismissed, directing the applicant to surrender within two weeks.

Complying with the same, the applicant surrendered on 15.04.2025, and is in custody since Devkumar Uchariya vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 7 August, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/120433248/

sentences.text: On merits, it is submitted that while granting the first bail, this Court had already considered in detail the nature of allegations and the conduct of the prosecutrix, including the fact that even after alleged acid administration and sexual assault, the prosecutrix had willingly accompanied the applicant to a guest house on 12.02.2023, which casts doubt over the prosecution story.
Further, the complaint was lodged only after the applicant's marriage was fixed, which raises serious questions about the timing and motive of the complaint.
Learned counsel also submitted that despite several months having passed, the prosecutrix has not appeared for examination before the trial Court, delaying the trial.
The applicant has remained in custody for nearly four months post-surrender, which constitutes a change in circumstance.
Therefore, the applicant may be released on bail.

Learned Public Prosecutor and the counsel for the complainant had opposed the application,
submitting that the allegations are serious in nature, involving repeated sexual assaults, and the applicant had earlier misused the liberty granted to him.

They contended that the applicant is not entitled to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-GWL:16827 3 MCRC-32227-2025 benefit of bail again, as his past conduct indicates the possibility of him interfering with the trial and influencing witnesses if released, and also since bail rejection order had been affirmed by the Apex Court, no case of fresh bail is made out.

Upon hearing learned counsel for the parties and perusal of the record, it is noted that: The applicant was earlier granted bail on merits, and while granting the same, the Court had already considered significant aspects of the case including the behavior of the prosecutrix post-alleged incident, which rendered the prosecution version prima facie doubtful.
The cancellation of earlier bail was not on the basis of merits of the present case, but due to violation of bail conditions due to commission of another offence.
In that matter, charge sheet has been filed, and the applicant is facing trial.
The applicant complied with the directions of the Apex Court and had surrendered on 15.04.2025, and has since remained in custody for nearly four months.
It is also a matter of record that the prosecutrix has not appeared for her examination before the trial Court, and trial proceedings have not made substantial progress.
The applicant has undertaken to abide by all conditions imposed by the Court and not to influence any witness or tamper with the evidence.

Considering the totality of circumstances, including change in circumstance, delay in trial, and previous judicial observations on merits, this Court is of the view that the applicant deserves to be enlarged on bail.
Accordingly, without commenting on the merits of the case, the present application is allowed.
